answer: We define a mechanism where agents post dynamic opportunity-cost bonds calibrated to a karst topography of transaction costs, rendering identity multiplication a relic of inefficient protocols. By mapping agent actions to a subgame-perfect slashing matrix, we force a river of liquidity to flow toward honest equilibria. We prove the expected payoff of Sybil replication is strictly negative, ensuring that Nash equilibrium convergence remains robust against adversarial agents.
